column1: # ENV-DOORS — the product items that read the process environment (T-DIAGNOSTIC-DOORS-AT-THE-ENTRY).
# A `BT_` variable is the person's shell speaking to one run of the program, so it is read once, at
# the program's entry, and handed down; a library never reads one at the moment of use.
# crates/bt-source/tests/env_doors.rs reads every product item of every first-party package and holds
# it to this list as an EQUALITY keyed by (file, item): every item that reads a `BT_` name in a
# supported shape, or holds a shape the guard's grammar refuses, has exactly its row; `names` is
# exactly the `BT_` names it reads (comma-separated, `-` for none); `refused` is exactly the number
# of refused shapes in it; a row whose item reads nothing is stale. See docs/ARCHITECTURE-GUARDS.md,
# An `item` of `-` is a read outside every item bt-source indexes: a static's initializer, a
# module-level macro or `use`; such reads in one file share the row.
#   entry     a program's entry: bt-app's one reader of the recording and trace doors, and the
#   door      a behaviour or test door still read where it is used; `ticket` names the follow-up
#             that moves it to the entry;
#   unjudged  a refused shape that reads no `BT_` door; `reason` says what it reads, and the follow-up
#             T-ENV-UNJUDGED-ROWS rewrites each into a supported shape or a parameter.
# THIS LIST ONLY SHRINKS (scripts/ci/check-env-doors.ps1 against the merge base). A new reader is
# moved to the entry, never listed; an added row (or a row that reads more) is refused, and the
# grammar is not widened to quiet a refusal.
# module: the module the item is written in (`-` for a read in no item), held equal to the tree like the
# rest; with it, a row moved to another file and module is that row moved, not one added
